title: Ephemeral Secrets Broker — Issuance & SIEM Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook documents the operational procedures and SIEM mapping for the Ephemeral Secrets Broker (ESB) workflow: issuance, enforcement, automatic evidence capture, and break-glass for vendor/external keys and short-lived machine credentials. It ties RBAC v2 decisions to audit schema fields and describes how evidence is exported into the enterprise SIEM to support compliance and forensic needs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to secrets issued via ESB (internal ephemeral tokens, short-lived SSH certs, short TTL API keys).
- Persistent long-lived secrets (service principals, long-term certificates) are covered elsewhere.
- ESB integrates with central Vault, RBAC v2, and the Audit Exporter service that forwards to our SIEM cluster.
- Operators have access to the Security Console and can run the remediation scripts in /infra/scripts (ops repo).

Quick definitions:
- Issuance: on-demand minting of a secret with TTL and metadata bound to a subject (user/service) and a role.
- Break-glass: out-of-band process to create credentials with elevated TTL or access when normal flows fail, with strict manual approval.
- Evidence bundle: packaged artifacts (audit log slice, request/response snapshot, signer SSO logs, related Jira ticket) used for post-incident review.

RBAC v2 mapping (operational notes):
- Roles are evaluated by ESB against RBAC v2 policy. The ESB request payload must include: subject_id, subject_type, requested_role, requested_ttl_seconds, justification_id (optional).
- Deny overrides: any explicit deny in RBAC v2 must be surfaced immediately in ESB responses with a denial_code and denial_reason.
- Role-to-capability mapping must be stored in policy registry and referenced by policy_id in audit logs.

Issuance flow (normal):
1) Client POST /esb/v1/issue with JSON body: subject_id, role, requested_ttl.
2) ESB validates caller token, resolves subject with RBAC v2, and evaluates policy.
3) If allowed, ESB mints secret in central Vault under path: secret/esb/<request_id>.
4) ESB returns ephemeral secret payload with: token, ttl_seconds, expires_at, rotated=false, request_id.
5) ESB emits an audit event to Audit Exporter synchronously (see audit schema below).
6) Audit Exporter forwards enriched event to SIEM (elk/graylog) with metadata tags for correlation and evidence retention windows.

Key enforcement controls:
- Max TTL per role: enforced in policy (e.g., role_db_read = 15m max).
- Auto-rotation: ESB can issue a rotated flag for secrets created as part of a rotation flow.
- Scope binding: every secret must be bound to a resource list or wildcard (resource_selector).
- Token usage limits: token can be revoked early via ESB revoke API; revocations push immediate audit events.

Audit log schema (plain-text representation used by Audit Exporter):
- event_time: ISO8601 timestamp
- event_id: UUID v4
- service: esb
- service_version: v1.12.0
- action: issue | revoke | rotate | break_glass_request | break_glass_grant
- subject_id: <user|service>:id
- subject_type: user | service | external_vendor
- requested_role: policy role string
- policy_id: policy registry id used for decision
- decision: allow | deny | contingent (requires approval)
- decision_reason: free text (policy hit, deny rule id, approval id)
- request_id: ESB-generated id for correlation
- secret_path: vault path (if created) or null
- ttl_seconds: integer
- expires_at: ISO8601 or null
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- evidence_refs: list of artifact ids (comma-separated in the flat log)
- correlation_tags: comma-separated tags for SIEM grouping (e.g., team:payments, env:prod)
- request_payload_hash: sha256 hex
- operator_id: system actor that performed action (if applicable)
- approval_id: id of manual approval (if break-glass)

Sample single-line JSON event (what SIEM receives):
{"event_time":"2025-01-03T13:22:11Z","event_id":"123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426655440000","service":"esb","action":"issue","subject_id":"user:olivia","subject_type":"user","requested_role":"db_read_limited","policy_id":"policy-117","decision":"allow","request_id":"req-9f8e","secret_path":"secret/esb/req-9f8e","ttl_seconds":900,"expires_at":"2025-01-03T13:37:11Z","outcome":"success","evidence_refs":"evidence-req-9f8e","correlation_tags":"team:platform,env:prod","request_payload_hash":"a3f5...","operator_id":"system"}

Evidence automation (how we collect and store):
- Trigger: every issue/revoke/rotate/break_glass_grant emits an audit event with evidence_refs pointing to the Evidence Bundle Store (EBS).
- Evidence Bundle composition: 
  * audit_event.json (the event shown above)
  * request_http.txt (raw request headers + body SHA only if PII-free; otherwise store pointer to secured request archive)
  * vault_response.txt (metadata only, not secret values)
  * sso_signin_slice.log (if user interactive)
  * approval_record.pdf (for break-glass)
  * jira_ticket.txt (linked ticket snapshot)
- Automation pipeline: Audit Exporter -> Evidence Bundler -> S3 (encrypted, separate bucket) -> SIEM indexer receives reference and retention metadata.

SIEM export mapping guidance:
- Use the event_id as the SIEM primary key.
- Map correlation_tags to SIEM fields: team, env, criticality.
- Indexed fields: event_time, action, subject_id, policy_id, decision, expires_at, operator_id, approval_id.
- Keep non-indexed free-text fields for retention but avoid indexing long PII fields.

Break-glass procedure (operational checklist):
A) When to use: emergency access needed for incident response if normal issuance path unavailable and time-critical remediation required.
B) Preconditions:
  - Phone approval from SOC lead AND written approval in approval system (approval_id).
  - Create Jira incident ticket and link it to request (JIRA-INC-####).
C) Steps to perform break-glass issuance:
  1) Operator opens Security Console -> Break-Glass -> Create request and attach justification + approval_id.
  2) ESB records a provisional event: action=break_glass_request, decision=contingent.
  3) SOC lead approves in approval system; approval_id recorded.
  4) Operator completes request; ESB performs mint with elevated TTL but marks secret as break_glass=true and sets forced_review_at (timestamp 7 days).
  5) ESB emits audit events: break_glass_grant + evidence_refs with approval artifacts.
  6) Immediately notify SIEM and escalate to on-call.
D) Post-break-glass mandatory tasks:
  - Forced rotation of any secrets issued via break-glass no later than forced_review_at.
  - Run evidence collection playbook: /infra/scripts/collect_esb_evidence.sh <request_id> and upload to Compliance S3.
  - SOC performs a 72-hour and 7-day review documented on Jira ticket.

Revocation/rotation recovery steps (if a secret is suspected):
1) Run esb revoke --request-id <request_id> --actor <operator> ; this triggers a revoke audit event.
2) Run esb rotate --resource <resource> --policy-id <policy> to reissue with default TTLs.
3) Confirm revocation events in SIEM within 5 minutes (correlation_tags=team:* and request_id).
4) If Vault shows lingering sessions, run vault session-invalidate <session-id> for related sessions and log session teardown to evidence bundle.

Playbook scripts and operators notes (short pointers):
- collect_esb_evidence.sh: takes request_id, queries Audit Exporter for all events with request_id, downloads linked artifacts from Evidence Bundle Store, packages them and uploads to s3://compliance-evidence/esb/YYYY/MM/DD/<request_id>.zip
- quick_audit_search: use the SIEM shortcut saved search "ESB-RequestID" and paste request_id. Filters: last 30m, action in (issue,revoke,rotate,break_glass_*).
- emergency_revoke: if secrets are used by prod automation, run revoke with cascade flag and alert infra-automation channel.

Monitoring and alerting knobs:
- SIEM rule: create an alert when break_glass_grant occurs in prod and approval_id is missing or approval record older than 1 hour.
- SIEM rule: high rate of issue events for a single subject (>10 in 1m) triggers throttling and human review.
- Evidence retention: default 1 year for ephemeral issuance evidence; 7 years for break-glass bundles (per audit policy).

Sourcing and references:
- RBAC v2 design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Design
- ESB design notes and API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/secrets-broker/blob/main/README.md
- Audit Exporter and SIEM mapping: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Audit+Exporter+Mapping

Open questions / TODOs (engineering/security sync):
- Decide canonical maximum TTLs for cross-team roles (action item with product infra).
- Add deterministic, machine-readable approval receipts to Approval System so Audit Exporter can attach certs directly.
- Implement masking policies in request archives to avoid storing PII in evidence bundles.

Appendix: forensic checklist for incident reviewers:
- Confirm audit_event.json exists and matches SIEM entry.
- Verify request_payload_hash matches raw request archive hash.
- Validate approval_id and approval_record.pdf integrity (signed).
- Check policy_id and RBAC v2 policy version to identify when policy changed relative to issuance.
- Ensure forced_review_at actions executed (rotation or revoke).

Contact and escalation:
- Primary owner: Riya Desai (security team) — DM on Slack or page via on-call rota.
- SOC lead: Marcus Liu
- ESB on-call: infra-automation rotation

Status: in_review — awaiting SOC/Infra signoff on TTLs and SIEM field types.
